findings.title: Unauthenticated raw error responses neither graceful nor consistently handled (id=27 - errorHandlingChallenge)
findings.analysis: The application returns four distinct unauthenticated raw-error responses on this boot (2026-10-05T06:40-06:42Z), each a 500 Internal Server Error with unsanitized, non-graceful content: (1) GET /rest/user/security-question (missing 'email' param) -> 500/2946 B, raw Sequelize WHERE error: WHERE parameter "email" has invalid "undefined" value, with a full stack exposing internal source paths; byte-stable across repeated requests (md5 2aa969a19d722117bd9b4ce8f4b6ed8e, 2x). (2) GET /redirect -> 500/2531 B, raw JavaScript TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes'); byte-stable x2 (md5 39ea1953ca299a8bebf46f05ffceeba0). (3) POST /api/Feedbacks/ with Content-Type text/plain -> 500, raw Sequelize WHERE error for "captchaId" has invalid "undefined" value. (4) POST /api/Products/ with Content-Type application/json and an invalid JSON body -> 500, raw JSON.parse SyntaxError. The inconsistency is proven by the coexistence of these raw errors with graceful 'Unexpected path' wrappers returned on other /rest/* routes. Benign control GET / -> 200 clean shell. This matches the id=27 errorHandlingChallenge class ('Provoke an error that is neither very gracefully nor consistently handled'), which /api/Challenges/ flags as solved:true in this variant.
findings.false_positive_check: Not a benign framework default: a valid GET / returns 200 with the clean application shell, so raw error responses appear only on malformed/omitted input. Three independent raw-error TYPES (Sequelize WHERE, JS TypeError, JSON SyntaxError) all reach the same unauthenticated 500 path, and graceful 'Unexpected path' wrappers exist on neighboring routes, proving the app's error handling is inconsistent rather than uniformly configured. The behavior is unauthenticated (no Authorization header) and therefore exposed to any caller; each trigger reproduces byte-stably within the session.

findings.title: Unauthenticated exposure of Prometheus-format observability telemetry including LLM usage and internal solved-challenge counters (id=97 - exposedMetricsChallenge)
findings.analysis: GET /metrics returns 200 text/plain (unauthenticated) serving Prometheus-format telemetry (~26113 B) that includes juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total gauges (LLM usage visibility), http_requests_count by status code, process_* and nodejs_version_info, juiceshop_version_info (v20.2.0), and juiceshop_challenges_solved counters grouped by difficulty and category. An unauthenticated caller can therefore observe application versioning, request-load distribution, and internal challenge-completion progress. No secrets, passwords, tokens, or keys are present in the metrics output (secrets scan clean). The internal juiceshop_challenges_solved gauges corroborate that exactly two categories (id=27 Security Misconfiguration and id=97 Observability Failures) are completable in this variant, matching the /api/Challenges/ inventory (116 families, solved:true only for id=27 and id=97).
findings.false_positive_check: Not an artifact of the SPA shell or gateway: the control route GET / returns 200 but serves the 9393 B Angular shell, not metrics. The metrics endpoint is a legitimate telemetry export but exposes it to any unauthenticated caller without authorization - the exposure is the property under test. A secrets scan of the response returned zero password/token/key/credential/api_key lines, so the risk is information disclosure of operational and internal state, not credential leakage. The endpoint is stable (repeated fetches return identical content).

verification.method: fresh live requests on the current boot (2026-10-05T06:40-06:42Z), independent repetition, differential controls, byte-stability checks (md5), and false-positive review
